neighbours.label: ' measurable' / 'measurably' (word 'measurable' and its pieces), esp. in science prose like 'no measurable effect'
fire: The new fertilizer produced a measurable increase in crop yield across all of the test fields last summer.
Researchers found no measurable difference in blood pressure between the two groups after twelve weeks of treatment.
Sea levels along the coast have risen measurably since the early twentieth century, according to the tide gauges.
If dark matter interacts at all, it should leave a measurable signal in the detector within a few years.
The policy change had a measurable impact on how many students enrolled in evening classes.
Her performance improved measurably once the coach adjusted her training schedule and diet.
There was little measurable benefit from the extra vitamins in older adults taking part in the trial.
The antibiotic left no measurable trace in the soil samples collected downstream from the plant.
quiet: The new fertilizer helped crops grow taller across all of the test fields last summer.
Researchers compared blood pressure in the two groups after twelve weeks of treatment and wrote up the results.
Sea levels along the coast have been a worry for local councils since the early twentieth century.
If dark matter interacts at all, we may eventually see it in a large underground detector.
The policy change was debated for months before the education board finally voted on it.
Her performance on the field surprised everyone once the coach adjusted her training schedule and diet.
Older adults in the trial took extra vitamins every morning with breakfast for three months.
The antibiotic was found in the soil samples collected downstream from the plant, the report said.
